Romans.author: Paul the apostle.
Romans.audience: Christians in Rome, including both Jewish and Gentile believers.
Romans.purpose: To explain the gospel, address tensions between Jewish and Gentile believers, and prepare for Paul's hoped-for mission farther west.
Romans.theme: God's righteousness is revealed in the gospel: all have sinned, justification is by faith, new life comes through the Spirit, and Jews and Gentiles are united in God's saving plan.
Romans.summary: Romans gives Paul's fullest sustained explanation of the gospel, moving from universal sin to justification, new life, Israel's place in God's purposes, and practical life in a diverse church.

movements.title: Human Sin and Justification
movements.description: Paul argues that both Gentiles and Jews are under sin and that justification comes through faith apart from works of the law.

movements.title: New Life in Christ and the Spirit
movements.description: Believers are united with Christ, freed from sin's dominion, and empowered by the Spirit.

movements.title: Israel, Church Unity, and Christian Practice
movements.description: Paul wrestles with Israel's place in God's plan and calls the Roman church to humble, unified, sacrificial living.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: The apostle writing to a church he has not yet visited.

keyFigures.name: Abraham
keyFigures.description: Presented as the father of all who believe, justified by faith before circumcision.

keyFigures.name: Adam
keyFigures.description: Contrasted with Christ: through Adam came sin and death, through Christ grace and life.

keyFigures.name: Phebe
keyFigures.description: A servant (or deacon) of the church at Cenchrea, likely the letter's carrier.

keyFigures.name: Priscilla and Aquila
keyFigures.description: Coworkers of Paul who risked their lives for him and host a church.

keyFigures.name: Tertius
keyFigures.description: The scribe who wrote down the letter.

1 Corinthians.author: Paul the apostle.
1 Corinthians.purpose: To correct divisions, immorality, lawsuits, disorderly worship, and confusion about marriage, spiritual gifts, the Lord's Supper, and resurrection.
1 Corinthians.theme: The cross reshapes Christian identity, relationships, worship, freedom, and hope.
1 Corinthians.summary: Paul responds to reports and questions from a gifted but divided church. He repeatedly redirects believers from status and self-interest toward holiness, love, mutual edification, and resurrection hope.

movements.title: Divisions and Moral Problems Addressed
movements.description: Paul confronts factions, pride, sexual immorality, and lawsuits.

movements.title: Questions about Christian Life and Worship
movements.description: Marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's Supper, head coverings, and spiritual gifts are discussed.

movements.title: Resurrection Defended
movements.description: Paul insists that bodily resurrection is central to the gospel and Christian hope.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: The church's founder, writing to correct and instruct it.

keyFigures.name: Sosthenes
keyFigures.description: Named as co-sender of the letter.

keyFigures.name: Apollos
keyFigures.description: A gifted teacher whom some in Corinth set up as a rival to Paul.

keyFigures.name: Cephas (Peter)
keyFigures.description: Another leader around whom a faction forms.

keyFigures.name: Chloe's people
keyFigures.description: Members of a household who report the church's quarrels to Paul.

keyFigures.name: Timothy
keyFigures.description: Paul's coworker, sent to remind the church of Paul's ways.

keyFigures.name: Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus
keyFigures.description: Corinthian believers who visit Paul and refresh his spirit.

2 Corinthians.author: Paul the apostle.
2 Corinthians.purpose: To defend Paul's apostolic ministry, explain the character of Christian ministry, encourage reconciliation, and complete a collection for believers in Jerusalem.
2 Corinthians.theme: God's power is displayed through weakness, suffering, integrity, generosity, and reconciliation.
2 Corinthians.summary: Paul speaks with unusual personal openness about suffering, ministry, reconciliation, generosity, and his contested relationship with the Corinthians.

movements.title: Ministry through Weakness
movements.description: Paul explains affliction, comfort, integrity, and the treasure of the gospel in fragile human vessels.

movements.title: Collection for Jerusalem
movements.description: Paul urges generous, willing participation in relief for needy believers.

movements.title: Defense of Apostleship
movements.description: Paul confronts rival claims and argues that true apostolic authority is marked by suffering, weakness, and dependence on Christ.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Defends his ministry and expresses deep affection for the church.

keyFigures.name: Timothy
keyFigures.description: Named as co-sender.

keyFigures.name: Titus
keyFigures.description: Paul's coworker who brings encouraging news from Corinth and helps organize the collection.

keyFigures.name: The “very chiefest apostles”
keyFigures.description: Rival teachers who boast in credentials and undermine Paul.

keyFigures.name: The offender
keyFigures.description: An unnamed person disciplined by the church whom Paul now urges them to forgive.

Galatians.author: Paul the apostle.
Galatians.audience: Churches in Galatia, in central Asia Minor.
Galatians.purpose: To oppose pressure on Gentile believers to adopt circumcision and law observance as necessary for covenant inclusion and to defend justification by faith in Christ.
Galatians.theme: In Christ, people are justified by faith and live by the Spirit rather than relying on works of the law for covenant status.
Galatians.summary: Paul strongly defends the gospel he preached, argues from Abraham and Scripture, and calls believers to use freedom not for self-indulgence but for Spirit-shaped love.

movements.title: Paul Defends His Gospel
movements.description: Paul recounts his calling and confrontations over Gentile inclusion.

movements.title: Faith, Promise, and Law
movements.description: Paul argues that God's promise to Abraham precedes the law and that justification comes through faith.

movements.title: Freedom and Life in the Spirit
movements.description: Believers are called to stand firm in freedom and bear the fruit of the Spirit through love.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Defends the gospel of grace and his apostolic calling.

keyFigures.name: Peter (Cephas)
keyFigures.description: Confronted by Paul at Antioch for withdrawing from table fellowship with Gentiles.

keyFigures.name: James
keyFigures.description: The Lord's brother and a pillar of the Jerusalem church.

keyFigures.name: Barnabas
keyFigures.description: Paul's companion, who is briefly drawn into the withdrawal at Antioch.

keyFigures.name: Titus
keyFigures.description: A Gentile believer who was not compelled to be circumcised.

keyFigures.name: Abraham
keyFigures.description: Paul's chief example of justification by faith and the recipient of the promise.

keyFigures.name: Hagar and Sarah
keyFigures.description: Used in an allegory contrasting slavery and freedom.

Ephesians.author: Paul the apostle, writing as a prisoner (Ephesians 3:1; 4:1).
Ephesians.audience: Christians in and around Ephesus, possibly intended as a circular letter for multiple churches.
Ephesians.purpose: To describe God's cosmic plan in Christ and call the church to live in unity, holiness, love, and spiritual strength.
Ephesians.theme: God unites all things in Christ and creates one new people who should live in unity, holiness, love, and spiritual maturity.
Ephesians.summary: Ephesians moves from what God has done in Christ—election, redemption, grace, reconciliation—to how believers should live as one body, one family, and one people equipped for spiritual conflict.

movements.title: Spiritual Blessings in Christ
movements.description: Paul praises God's saving purpose and grace in Christ.

movements.title: Jew and Gentile United
movements.description: Christ's work creates one new humanity and one household of God.

movements.title: Walk Worthy and Stand Firm
movements.description: The church is called to unity, holiness, transformed relationships, and spiritual armor.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes as a prisoner for the Lord.

keyFigures.name: Tychicus
keyFigures.description: A faithful minister sent to carry the letter and report on Paul.

Philippians.author: Paul the apostle, writing with Timothy named in the greeting.
Philippians.purpose: To thank the Philippians for support, encourage unity and joy amid suffering, and present Christ's humility as the pattern for Christian life.
Philippians.theme: Joy and faithful unity are possible in suffering when believers center life on Christ's humility, resurrection, and coming victory.
Philippians.summary: Philippians is a warm letter of gratitude and encouragement. Paul discusses imprisonment, Christ's self-emptying humility, warnings against false confidence, and contentment in every circumstance.

movements.title: Gospel Advances through Imprisonment
movements.description: Paul explains that his confinement has unexpectedly helped spread the gospel.

movements.title: Christ's Humility as the Model
movements.description: The famous Christ hymn calls believers to self-giving unity and obedience.

movements.title: Pressing On and Learning Contentment
movements.description: Paul rejects confidence in status, pursues Christ, and explains contentment in plenty or need.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes from imprisonment with joy and gratitude.

keyFigures.name: Timothy
keyFigures.description: Co-sender, commended for genuine concern for the church.

keyFigures.name: Epaphroditus
keyFigures.description: The Philippians' messenger to Paul, who nearly died in service.

keyFigures.name: Euodias and Syntyche
keyFigures.description: Two women who labored with Paul and are urged to agree in the Lord.

Colossians.author: Paul the apostle, with Timothy named in the greeting (Colossians 1:1; 4:18).
Colossians.purpose: To affirm the supremacy and sufficiency of Christ and warn against teachings that diminish his centrality.
Colossians.theme: Christ is supreme over creation and the church, and believers are complete in him.
Colossians.summary: Colossians presents an exalted picture of Christ, warns against spiritual systems that promise fullness elsewhere, and calls believers to put off the old life and put on a Christlike one.

movements.title: Supremacy of Christ
movements.description: A major hymn presents Christ as image of the invisible God, creator, sustainer, and head of the church.

movements.title: Warnings against Rival Spiritual Claims
movements.description: Believers are told not to be captured by teachings centered on regulations, asceticism, or angelic powers.

movements.title: New Life in Christ
movements.description: Practical exhortations address character, relationships, households, prayer, and witness.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes from prison to a church he has not visited.

keyFigures.name: Timothy
keyFigures.description: Named as co-sender.

keyFigures.name: Epaphras
keyFigures.description: Founder of the Colossian church, who prays earnestly for them.

keyFigures.name: Tychicus and Onesimus
keyFigures.description: Sent to deliver the letter and report on Paul.

keyFigures.name: Aristarchus, Mark, Luke, and Demas
keyFigures.description: Companions of Paul who send greetings.

keyFigures.name: Archippus
keyFigures.description: Encouraged to complete the ministry he has received.

1 Thessalonians.author: Paul the apostle, with Silvanus and Timothy named in the greeting (1 Thessalonians 1:1).
1 Thessalonians.purpose: To encourage a young persecuted church, affirm their faith, call for holy living, and clarify hope concerning believers who had died before Christ's return.
1 Thessalonians.theme: Faithful Christian life combines hope in Christ's return, holiness, mutual love, and perseverance under pressure.
1 Thessalonians.summary: Paul warmly remembers the Thessalonians' conversion, encourages sexual holiness and brotherly love, and reassures them that deceased believers will share fully in Christ's return.

movements.title: Conversion and Perseverance Remembered
movements.description: Paul recalls the church's turning from idols and endurance under persecution.

movements.title: Holy Living Encouraged
movements.description: Believers are called to sexual holiness, brotherly love, and responsible work.

movements.title: Hope in Christ's Return
movements.description: Paul comforts the church regarding deceased believers and urges readiness for the day of the Lord.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes with deep affection to a young church he had to leave abruptly.

keyFigures.name: Silvanus (Silas)
keyFigures.description: Paul's coworker in founding the church; named as co-sender.

keyFigures.name: Timothy
keyFigures.description: Sent back to strengthen the church; returns with a good report of their faith and love.

2 Thessalonians.author: Paul the apostle, with Silvanus and Timothy named in the greeting (2 Thessalonians 1:1; 3:17).
2 Thessalonians.purpose: To encourage persecuted believers, correct confusion about the day of the Lord, and address idleness within the community.
2 Thessalonians.theme: Persevere faithfully, do not be deceived about the end, and continue responsible Christian living.
2 Thessalonians.summary: 2 Thessalonians reassures suffering believers that God will judge evil, warns that certain events must precede the day of the Lord, and commands disorderly members to work quietly.

movements.title: Perseverance under Persecution
movements.description: Paul praises endurance and points toward God's righteous judgment.

movements.title: Correction about the Day of the Lord
movements.description: The church is told not to panic and is given difficult teaching about the falling away and the man of sin.

movements.title: Work and Discipline
movements.description: Paul addresses those who have become idle and disruptive.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes to correct confusion about the day of the Lord.

keyFigures.name: Silvanus and Timothy
keyFigures.description: Named as co-senders.

keyFigures.name: The man of sin
keyFigures.description: A figure of rebellion who must be revealed before the day of the Lord.

1 Timothy.author: Traditionally attributed to Paul and addressed to Timothy; some modern scholars debate Pauline authorship.
1 Timothy.audience: Timothy in Ephesus and the churches under his care.
1 Timothy.purpose: To guide church order, sound teaching, leadership qualifications, worship, care for vulnerable members, and faithful ministry.
1 Timothy.theme: Healthy churches require sound teaching, godly leadership, disciplined care, and lives that match the gospel.
1 Timothy.summary: 1 Timothy combines pastoral guidance with instructions about doctrine, prayer, leadership, widows, elders, money, and Timothy's own conduct.

movements.title: False Teaching Confronted
movements.description: Timothy is urged to resist speculative teaching and preserve the gospel's aim of love and good conscience.

movements.title: Worship and Leadership Ordered
movements.description: Instructions address prayer, men and women in worship, overseers, and deacons.

movements.title: Pastoral Care and Godly Conduct
movements.description: The letter covers widows, elders, wealth, discipline, and Timothy's example.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes to instruct his coworker on church life and leadership.

keyFigures.name: Timothy
keyFigures.description: Paul's 'true child in the faith,' left in Ephesus to confront false teaching.

keyFigures.name: Hymenaeus and Alexander
keyFigures.description: Men who have shipwrecked their faith and been disciplined.

2 Timothy.author: Traditionally attributed to Paul and addressed to Timothy; some modern scholars debate Pauline authorship.
2 Timothy.audience: Timothy, with wider relevance for church leaders and believers.
2 Timothy.purpose: To strengthen Timothy for faithful ministry amid suffering, false teaching, and Paul's approaching death.
2 Timothy.theme: Guard the gospel, endure suffering, handle Scripture faithfully, and finish the race with perseverance.
2 Timothy.summary: 2 Timothy is personal and urgent. Paul calls Timothy to courage, disciplined endurance, faithful teaching, Scripture-shaped ministry, and confidence that the gospel cannot be imprisoned.

movements.title: Guard the Gospel
movements.description: Timothy is urged not to be ashamed and to entrust sound teaching to reliable people.

movements.title: Difficult Times and Scripture
movements.description: Paul warns about corrupt teachers and highlights the usefulness of God-breathed Scripture.

movements.title: Final Charge and Farewell
movements.description: Timothy is told to preach the word; Paul reflects that he has fought the good fight and finished the race.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes from prison, expecting his death, with a final charge.

keyFigures.name: Timothy
keyFigures.description: Urged to guard the gospel and endure suffering.

keyFigures.name: Lois and Eunice
keyFigures.description: Timothy's grandmother and mother, known for their sincere faith.

keyFigures.name: Onesiphorus
keyFigures.description: Searched for Paul in Rome and was not ashamed of his chains.

keyFigures.name: Hymenaeus and Philetus
keyFigures.description: Teachers who claim the resurrection has already happened.

keyFigures.name: Demas
keyFigures.description: A coworker who deserts Paul because he loves this present world.

keyFigures.name: Luke and Mark
keyFigures.description: Luke alone remains with Paul; Mark is requested as useful for ministry.

keyFigures.name: Alexander the coppersmith
keyFigures.description: A man who did Paul great harm and opposed his message.

Titus.author: Traditionally attributed to Paul and addressed to Titus; some modern scholars debate Pauline authorship.
Titus.purpose: To organize churches with qualified leaders, oppose false teaching, and connect sound doctrine with good works.
Titus.theme: Grace trains God's people to live self-controlled, upright, productive lives that make the gospel attractive.
Titus.summary: Titus instructs the appointment of elders, correction of false teachers, practical teaching for different groups, and a strong emphasis on good works flowing from grace.

movements.title: Elders Appointed
movements.description: Titus is instructed to establish qualified leadership in Cretan churches.

movements.title: Sound Doctrine Produces Godly Living
movements.description: Different age and social groups are taught conduct consistent with grace.

movements.title: Grace and Good Works
movements.description: Believers are reminded that salvation comes by God's mercy and should result in lives devoted to doing good.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes to guide the organization of churches in Crete.

keyFigures.name: Titus
keyFigures.description: Paul's coworker, left in Crete to appoint elders and teach sound doctrine.

keyFigures.name: Zenas and Apollos
keyFigures.description: A lawyer and a teacher whom Titus is asked to help on their journey.

keyFigures.name: Artemas and Tychicus
keyFigures.description: Coworkers, one of whom Paul plans to send so Titus can join him at Nicopolis.

Philemon.author: Paul the apostle, with Timothy named in the greeting.
Philemon.audience: Philemon, Apphia, Archippus, and the church meeting in Philemon's house.
Philemon.purpose: To appeal for Onesimus, asking Philemon to receive him not merely as a slave but as a beloved brother in Christ.
Philemon.theme: The gospel transforms relationships by creating a new family identity in Christ that challenges status and demands costly reconciliation.
Philemon.summary: Paul sends Onesimus back to Philemon with a personal appeal grounded in love rather than coercion. He asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as he would receive Paul himself.

movements.title: Paul Gives Thanks for Philemon
movements.description: The letter opens by praising Philemon's love and faith.

movements.title: Appeal for Onesimus
movements.description: Paul pleads for Onesimus, now described as useful and beloved in the Lord.

movements.title: Receive Him as You Would Me
movements.description: Paul offers to cover any debt and appeals for reconciled fellowship.

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.description: Writes from prison with a personal appeal.

keyFigures.name: Philemon
keyFigures.description: A believer who hosts a church in his house and is Onesimus' master.

keyFigures.name: Onesimus
keyFigures.description: An enslaved man who has become a believer and whom Paul sends back as a brother.

keyFigures.name: Apphia and Archippus
keyFigures.description: Members of Philemon's household church, greeted in the opening.

keyFigures.name: Timothy
keyFigures.description: Named as co-sender.

keyFigures.name: Epaphras, Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke
keyFigures.description: Paul's companions who send greetings.
